messages:
alex: Hey — running into a weird one with redwoodctl localserve + profiles. I start localserve with --profile staging-e2e and after I authenticate the profile disappears from ~/.config/redwood/profiles.json. Anyone seen this?

priya: hmm can you paste the exact command + minimal logs (redwoodctl --version and the auth error)?

alex: sure:
```bash
$ redwoodctl --version
redwoodctl v0.9.3
$ redwoodctl localserve --profile staging-e2e --port 8080
Starting localserver...
Opening browser for device auth...
error: auth: failed to write credential cache: read-only file system
```
I tried catting profiles.json after the failure and it only has the default profile, my staging-e2e never gets written.

jon: are you on Linux? any chance XDG_CONFIG_HOME is pointed at a synced folder (dropbox/drive) or a mount with weird permissions?

alex: yep Ubuntu. Echoing XDG_CONFIG_HOME gives `/home/alex/GoogleDrive/config`, I actually symlinked ~/.config -> ~/GoogleDrive/config for convenience.

priya: ok that explains the read-only FS error — cloud clients sometimes lock or mount with restrictive flags. Try exporting XDG_CONFIG_HOME to a local dir and rerun login:
```bash
export XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$HOME/.config-local
mkdir -p $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/redwood
redwoodctl login --device-code --profile staging-e2e
```
If that works, you probably hit write failures when the auth flow tried to persist the profile.

alex: did that — login succeeded and profile saved. Verified with `jq .profiles ~/.config-local/redwood/profiles.json` and staging-e2e is there. Thanks! :tada:

sarah: can you paste the stderr from the original failure? curious if we should catch this and give a clearer error message in redwoodctl (instead of a generic read-only fs).

alex: paste below (trimmed):
```
2026-03-21T14:02:11Z ERROR auth: failed to write profile file: open /home/alex/GoogleDrive/config/redwood/profiles.json: permission denied
main.main()
\tcmd/redwoodctl/main.go:142
```

jon: yeah we should detect EACCES/EROFS and print a hint about XDG_CONFIG_HOME or fallback to $HOME/.redwood. I'll open a tiny PR to add that guard + link to docs about config location.

sarah: also add a note to the localserve docs recommending against symlinking ~/.config to cloud-synced mounts; helped a few folks before.

devex-bot: Created issue #412 in redwoodctl: "installer/localserve: add clear error when config dir is not writable (XDG_CONFIG_HOME on network/synced mounts)" — https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwoodctl/issues/412

alex: awesome — repro steps posted in the issue. One more thing: after the failed write, localserve left a stale device-code session and my subsequent login attempts timed out until I removed a lock file at ~/.config/redwood/device_auth.lock. Maybe add cleanup on error?

priya: good catch. please add that note to the issue, and include the commands you used to clear it.

alex: added commands + minimal repro to #412. Thanks all, good to know workaround.

sarah: triaging to devex backlog, label: cli, priority: p2.

alex: closing thread — local testing unblocked. :white_check_mark:
